Library trials overnight returns robot

By Imogen Treadgold

The central library in the fictional town of Harrowell has started trialling a small wheeled robot that collects returned books from the overnight drop box and sorts them on to trolleys before staff arrive in the morning.

The robot, which staff have named Dewey, follows a strip of reflective tape around the back office. It reads the barcode on each book, checks it in on the catalogue, and places it on one of five trolleys according to which floor it belongs on.

Library manager Felix Ambrose said the trial was about saving time at the start of the day rather than replacing anyone. "The first hour used to be spent just emptying the box," he said. "Now the team can open the doors and get straight to helping people."

Dewey is not perfect. During the first week it repeatedly tried to check in a cardboard box of donated jigsaws, and it has a habit of stopping completely when someone leaves a coat on the floor. The supplier has promised a software update to deal with both problems.

The trial will run until the end of the year, after which the council will decide whether to buy the robot outright or return it. Visitors can watch it at work through a window in the children's section on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

Regular borrowers interviewed outside the building were mostly enthusiastic, although one asked whether the robot would be issuing late fines. The library confirmed that it would not.
